test_title: PYST 2: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is used to measure a decent standard of living in HDI?

options.text: GDP per capita in PPP US Dollars

solution:
The Correct answer is __**GDP per capita in PPP US Dollars**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **GDP per capita in PPP (Purchasing Power Parity) US Dollars** is a crucial metric for assessing the **decent standard of living** as per the **Human Development Index (HDI)**.
 
• It represents the **average income** of an individual in a country, adjusted for the cost of living and inflation, making it a more accurate measure for international comparisons.
 
• The HDI, developed by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**, uses this metric to quantify the economic dimension of human development.
 
• The use of **PPP** ensures that the measure accounts for differences in the **cost of goods and services** between countries, rather than using nominal GDP which may not reflect true purchasing power.
 
• A higher **GDP per capita in PPP** generally indicates better access to resources, higher income levels, and improved **living standards**, which are key components of a decent standard of living.
 
• By incorporating this economic indicator, the HDI provides a more holistic view of development that goes beyond traditional measures like **economic growth** alone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Population density**__

 __
 
• **Population density** refers to the number of people per unit area (e.g., per square kilometer) of land.
 
• It is used to study the **distribution of populations** but does not directly measure the **standard of living**.
 
 
 
• **Monthly salary**__
 __
 
• **Monthly salary** is an individual-level income metric and does not account for broader economic factors like inflation or purchasing power in a country.
 
• It is not used in international comparisons to measure the **standard of living**.
 
 
 
• **Availability of luxury goods**__
 
 
• The **availability of luxury goods** reflects consumption patterns but is not a reliable indicator of overall living standards for an entire population.
 
• It is more associated with wealth distribution among a small segment of society rather than a universal measure of well-being.
